seasonal_guidance.optimalWindow: Late July through August, when the Access Creek gullies and Luna Col approach are mostly snow-free and the long days allow the traverse

July.reason: Snow melts off the Luna Col approach through the month; early July still has avalanche debris and a high Big Beaver crossing.

June.reason: The Ross Lake water taxi starts in mid-June, but Access Creek runs high and deep snow covers the gullies to Luna Col.

August.reason: Least snow on the loose descent to the saddle, the creek crossing is lowest, and long days suit the tower traverse.

October.reason: The water taxi runs until the end of the month, but early snow on the loose, chossy towers and short days make it serious.

September.reason: Still climbable in stable weather and the water taxi still runs, but shorter days make a forced bivy likelier.

gaps: Difficulty breakdown (physical/technical/exposure/commitment/routefinding) is a computed starting estimate derived from grade, pitch count, and route data on file -- not a researched or crowd-sourced rating. Users can blend in their own read via the UI.

approach_logistics.trailheadDirection: From the Ross Dam Trailhead on SR-20 near milepost 134, down to Ross Lake and the water-taxi/trail network

row.rope_note: A 50-60 m rope at minimum, for rappelling the 4th- and low-5th-class sections between the three towers. Plan on building and leaving anchors: the rock is chossy, solid placements are scarce, and the rappels on this traverse go off poor-quality anchors - so carry slings and rings to back them up. Each rappel you make on the way across makes retreat progressively harder.
row.corrections: Glacier travel gear also needed for the broader Fury approach, though not specific to this ridge traverse itself.

approach_variants.name: Climb East Fury first; the traverse starts on its summit
approach_variants.notes:
This route has no approach of its own in the ordinary sense. It is the connecting ridge between the two summits of Mount Fury, and the only way to arrive at its start is to have climbed East Fury, which is reached from the Ross Dam Trailhead by water taxi to Big Beaver Landing, the Big Beaver Creek Trail, the Access Creek bushwhack, Access Col, Luna Col and the Southeast Glacier.

Budget the East Fury ascent as a full day in its own right before this one begins, and note that the traverse is about half a kilometre of ridge, which says nothing useful about how long it takes.
hazards: Poor-quality anchors on chossy rock, with each rappel making retreat harder
A committing position on a ridge between two of the most remote summits in the range
Loose class 2-3 talus on the descent of East Fury's east side
The whole outing sits behind a full day's climb of East Fury and a multi-day approach
approach_variants.baseFinding:
THE BASE OF THIS ROUTE IS A SUMMIT, WHICH IS THE ONE THING ON A MOUNTAIN YOU CANNOT WALK PAST. You are at the start when you are standing on the top of East Fury with the ridge running west toward the West Peak. There is no gully to find, no bench to identify and no chance of starting the wrong line: if you are not on East Fury's summit, you have not started.

WHAT THAT MEANS IN PRACTICE, AND IT IS A DECISION RATHER THAN A LANDMARK: the commitment happens at the first rappel, not at the summit. Getting off each tower on the traverse means rappelling off poor-quality anchors on chossy rock, and EACH RAPPEL DOWN MAKES RETREAT PROGRESSIVELY HARDER. The place to decide whether the weather and the hour justify the traverse is on East Fury's summit, before the first pull.

WHAT GOING TOO FAR LOOKS LIKE, ON THE OTHER END: once off the traverse, the way home is back over East Fury and down its east side to the saddle on loose class 2-3 talus, then down the Southeast Glacier to Luna Col. Descending anywhere off the north side of the connecting ridge drops you into Luna Cirque, 2,400 ft below the col you camped at.

bivy.name: Luna Col bivy, Luna cross-country zone
bivy.notes: Open bivy ground on the col above the Luna Cirque, reached by leaving the Big Beaver trail near Access Creek and climbing trackless ground to Access Col. It is the working high camp for Mount Fury's west peak and for Luna Peak, with no established site — you camp on rock, heather or snow and pack everything out. The brush on the Access Creek approach, which forces a bank change around 3,700 ft, is the part parties consistently underestimate.
bivy.water: Snowmelt and small tarns only; expect to melt snow once the basin dries out late in the season
bivy.permit: Wilderness permit required for the Luna cross-country zone. WALK-UP ONLY — this zone cannot be reserved in advance, so it is claimed in person at Marblemount. A party that has already driven and boated in can still be turned away if the night's slots are gone; carry a fallback itinerary.
bivy.capacity: Party limit 6; up to 6 parties per night in the Luna zone

bivy.name: Luna Camp, Big Beaver Trail
bivy.notes: The standard staging camp for the Access Creek side of the Northern Pickets — Mount Fury's west peak and the Luna Cirque generally. Most parties take the Ross Lake water taxi to the Big Beaver landing near 1,600 ft and then walk eight to ten miles of nearly flat old-growth trail, so it functions as a first night rather than a destination. The climbers' path leaves the maintained trail roughly a mile and a half beyond and crosses Big Beaver Creek near the Access Creek confluence; whether that crossing is a log or a wade varies year to year and with runoff.
bivy.water: Big Beaver Creek runs beside camp — reliable all season
bivy.permit: NPS wilderness permit from the Marblemount Wilderness Information Center; trail-corridor camp, reservable on Recreation.gov or walk-up. CLOSED under the Luna Fire closure as of the park's August 2026 list — confirm current status before building a trip around it.
bivy.capacity: Two 4-person sites; party limit 4; pit toilet, food hang
